watchOut: The range for "mid-sized or super-mid-sized" is a single band, so it cannot tell you which of the two costs more.
feesNamed: Taxes and fees outside the U.S.
name: Mercury Jets
roleBasis: Its cost page says: "As a charter broker, Mercury Jets compares aircraft and rates across a global network of FAA Part 135-certified operators." Its homepage says it holds the ARGUS Certified Charter Broker designation.
summary: Charter broker that publishes hourly ranges by trip range and aircraft type, and lists the charges it leaves out of them.
differentiator: Its page says the rates cover aircraft, crew and fuel only and then lists what is extra: federal excise tax, segment fees, boarding and airport taxes, overnight fees, international handling and landing fees. That separation is explicit, where several providers blur it.
priceNote: Hourly ranges from $1,800 to $12,500 depending on aircraft. It also groups flights by distance: short range $1,800 to $3,500, mid range $3,500 to $6,500, long range $6,500 to $12,500.
operatorDisclosure: Says it works with FAA Part 135-certified operators and presents several aircraft options. The pages we read do not say whether the operator is named before booking.
bestFor: Buyers who want a clear list of what sits outside the hourly rate before asking for a quote.
skipIf: You want one rate per aircraft category. Two of its ranges cover two categories at once.
